title: A Clock for the Atlas
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1874, Ada Sandoval, an orphaned mapmaker's apprentice, secretly completes the atlas her master died for—an atlas that proves the drowned quarter of Saltmarsh was deliberately flooded by the victors of the civil war to erase a rebellious district and its people. When a census taker's probing questions reveal that the regime is hunting the atlas's original survey notes, Ada realizes she is the last living witness who can put the truth on record before official historians seal the lie forever. Gathering an unlikely found family—a disgraced archivist, a smuggler's widow, and the census taker himself, whose conscience turns against his employers—Ada races to authenticate the maps and publish them. The book ends with the atlas printed in secret and nailed to every church door in Vellamare on the anniversary of the flood; Ada is arrested but released when the crowd refuses to let her vanish, and she finally claims her name, her craft, and her place in the city she mapped.
about_author: Freya Dunmore is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed municipal maps in coastal archives. She writes historical fiction about the people history tried to leave off the page.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlives Us
chapters.summary: Ada Sandoval works late in the shuttered map shop, inking coastlines for the atlas her dead master left unfinished. Her POV establishes her careful invisibility: no papers, no surname spoken aloud. Emotional beat: quiet grief channeled into precision—she trusts lines more than people.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Elias Wren arrives with routine questions but lingers on where Ada learned her trade and under whose name. POV alternates Ada and Elias, who suspects she is undocumented but hesitates to report her. Emotional beat: first crack in Ada's armor; being seen feels like danger.

chapters.title: What the Water Took
chapters.summary: Ada visits the seawall above the drowned quarter of Saltmarsh, remembering her master's obsession with its flooding. Flashback reveals he claimed the government broke the levees deliberately. Emotional beat: mourning sharpening into purpose—the atlas is not just maps; it is testimony.

chapters.title: The Master's Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Searching the shop, Ada finds a locked drawer and inside, half-burned survey notes proving the levee was cut from the landward side. POV: Ada alone. Emotional beat: terror and vindication entwined—she now holds evidence worth killing for.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Smuggles
chapters.summary: Ada seeks out Marta Quill, a harbor widow who once moved contraband for her master, asking her to hide the notes. Marta agrees but warns that the Bureau of Records has been buying up private papers all winter. Emotional beat: the first thread of found family, offered gruffly.

chapters.title: Elias Files His Report
chapters.summary: Elias drafts his census report on the unnamed apprentice but cannot bring himself to submit it, haunted by his own brother's disappearance into a records purge years ago. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: conscience at war with duty and self-preservation.

chapters.title: Buyers at the Door
chapters.summary: A Bureau agent visits the map shop offering generous coin for 'any materials of the late Master Corvane.' Ada plays the ignorant servant while her heart hammers. Emotional beat: the hunt has begun; invisibility is failing faster than she planned.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Fell
chapters.summary: Marta introduces Ada to Odile Ferrant, a former state archivist dismissed for questioning the official flood record, now drunk and bitter in a garret. Odile confirms the notes' authenticity—and their worth. Emotional beat: reluctant mentorship begins; expertise meets desperation.

chapters.title: Learning to Be Counted
chapters.summary: Odile explains what it will take to make the evidence legally undeniable: provenance, witnesses, and publication before the regime's official history prints next spring. Ada balks—publication means exposure. Emotional beat: fear confronting the cost of justice.

chapters.title: Saltmarsh Rising
chapters.summary: At the tenth-anniversary flood memorial, forbidden mourners gather despite bans. Ada sketches faces, realizing survivors are living witnesses she could collect. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: from hiding among the grieving to organizing them.

chapters.title: The Census Taker Returns
chapters.summary: Elias comes back with a pretext, but really to warn Ada that her file was flagged. He lies to his supervisor for the first time. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: his defection begins—not heroism, but guilt finding a direction.

chapters.title: Provenance
chapters.summary: Odile teaches Ada how archives authenticate documents; they reconstruct the chain of custody for Corvane's notes using old receipts and a witness signature. Emotional beat: hope built methodically, line by line, like a map.

chapters.title: The Survivor of Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Ada tracks down Tam Osei, a lockkeeper who saw soldiers at the levee the night of the flood and has been silent for ten years out of fear. He neither agrees nor refuses. Emotional beat: the weight of survival guilt; testimony as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: A Raid on the Shop
chapters.summary: Bureau agents ransack the map shop while Ada hides the notes in Marta's smuggling boat. They take the finished plates but miss the drawer's true contents. Emotional beat: violation and loss—her master's art seized—but resolve hardens.

chapters.title: What Elias Knows
chapters.summary: Elias discovers the raid was ordered because of his own flagged report; his supervisor used him as a tracking hound. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: shame curdling into open rebellion—he brings Ada the Bureau's list of targeted papers.

chapters.title: The Found Family Assembles
chapters.summary: In Marta's kitchen over stew, Ada, Marta, Odile, Elias, and Tam form an uneasy compact: get the atlas and testimony published before the official history releases. Emotional beat: belonging, terrifying and warm; Ada accepts she cannot do this alone.

chapters.title: Copying the Atlas
chapters.summary: Working nights in the boathouse, the group hand-copies the master atlas so no single seizure can destroy it. Odile's hands shake; Marta keeps watch; Elias learns to rule lines. Emotional beat: purpose made physical—many hands making one truth.

chapters.title: Tam Decides
chapters.summary: Tam watches soldiers harass Saltmarsh orphans at the market and finally agrees to sign a sworn statement about the levee. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: ten years of silence breaking; grief converted to courage.

chapters.title: The Historian's Advance Copy
chapters.summary: Elias steals a proof of the regime's official history: it blames the flood on rebel sabotage, naming Saltmarsh's own defenders as culprits. Emotional beat: fury and urgency—the lie is elegant, printed, and nearly done.

chapters.title: Marta's Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: An old smuggling partner blackmails Marta, threatening to expose the group. She pays him with her late husband's boat rather than betray them. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: sacrifice without sentiment; family chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Elias is summoned and questioned about the census irregularities. He walks a razor's edge, confessing just enough incompetence to protect Ada. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: dread, and the strange freedom of having already chosen his side.

chapters.title: The Printer on Tanner's Row
chapters.summary: The group finds a printer willing to run the atlas—if paid enormously and kept ignorant of contents. Ada sells her master's silver and her own few treasures. Emotional beat: giving up the past to secure the future.

chapters.title: A Map of Every Door
chapters.summary: Ada designs the distribution plan as literally a map: which streets, which churches, which hours, who carries what. Emotional beat: her craft becomes strategy; the apprentice becomes the planner.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: The blackmailed partner sells information anyway; agents raid the boathouse. The copies survive hidden in pickle barrels, but Tam is taken. Emotional beat: guilt and panic—the cost of trust misplaced.

chapters.title: Prison Visit
chapters.summary: Through Marta's harbor contacts, Ada gets word to Tam: hold silence, help is coming. Elias risks everything passing a message through prison channels. POV alternating Ada/Elias. Emotional beat: loyalty tested at distance; helplessness fought with small brave acts.

chapters.title: Odile's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Odile falls ill; from her sickbed she drills Ada on authentication until Ada can defend every document alone. She gives Ada her archivist's seal. Emotional beat: transmission of legacy; the student becomes the keeper.

chapters.title: The Bureau Closes In
chapters.summary: Agents identify 'the Corvane apprentice' and circulate a sketch that looks unsettlingly like Ada. She must move safehouses, cutting her hair, changing her walk. Emotional beat: invisibility fully stripped away; identity reduced to a hunted face.

chapters.title: What Ada Is Willing to Lose
chapters.summary: Alone in a chapel loft, Ada confronts the endgame: publication means arrest, maybe the gallows. She decides the record matters more than her safety. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—justice outside the law demands a body to pay for it.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: The official history ships to booksellers; the group's printing finishes the same night. Race-day logistics snap into motion. Emotional beat: breathless momentum—two versions of truth racing to the same shelves.

chapters.title: Freeing Tam
chapters.summary: Marta engineers Tam's release by bribing a turnkey with the blackmailer's own hush money, turned against him. Tam walks free at dawn. Emotional beat: the found family striking back together; luck earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Night of Doors
chapters.summary: Climax begins: across Vellamare, couriers nail the atlas and sworn testimonies to church doors and customs-house walls. Ada herself posts the copy on the Bureau's own door. Emotional beat: exhilaration, terror, and the city waking to papered walls.

chapters.title: Morning Reading
chapters.summary: Vellamare wakes to the atlas; crowds gather at Saltmarsh's seawall reading aloud, weeping, arguing. Some officials quietly resign. POV shifts among citizens. Emotional beat: truth landing like a tide—undeniable once seen.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Agents seize Ada at the print shop. She does not run; she hands the arresting officer a copy of the atlas and asks him to read page forty before locking her up. Emotional beat: calm defiance; she has already won something no cell can undo.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: At Ada's hearing, Elias testifies openly, Tam gives his statement publicly, and Odile—carried in on a chair—authenticates the documents before the magistrates. Emotional beat: the courtroom transformed into the archive; witnesses becoming a chorus.

chapters.title: The Crowd Outside
chapters.summary: Thousands gathered outside refuse to disperse when a guilty verdict is read; printers begin running a second edition openly. The magistrates, fearing the street more than the ministry, suspend the sentence. Emotional beat: power shifting visibly from law to people.

chapters.title: Release
chapters.summary: Ada walks out into a crowd that knows her name and cheers it. Overwhelmed, she realizes she has gone from uncounted to unforgettable. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: belonging achieved at last—not granted, but claimed.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Shop
chapters.summary: Neighbors return the seized plates salvaged from Bureau storerooms; the map shop reopens with a new sign: Sandoval & Ferrant, Cartographers. Emotional beat: restoration with changed terms—her name on the door at last.

chapters.title: The Second Edition
chapters.summary: The expanded atlas publishes legally, with Saltmarsh restored to the maps and the survivors' names inscribed along its drowned streets. Emotional beat: grief given geography; memory made permanent.

chapters.title: Elias's Choice
chapters.summary: Elias resigns from the Bureau and takes work as the atlas project's registrar, documenting testimony for historians yet to come. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: redemption as vocation; the man who counted people now counts for them.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Atlas
chapters.summary: One year later, Ada installs a tide clock above the shop door, set to the hour the levee broke, so the city never forgets. She teaches apprentices—including Saltmarsh orphans—that every map is an argument about who belongs. Emotional beat: resolution and forward motion; the record kept, the family kept, the name kept.
